name: Mine customer language into a research packet
what: Gathers raw voice-of-customer material, reviews, support tickets, buyer interviews, site search terms and founder video, and turns it into one research packet strategists and copywriters draw angles and proof from.
encompasses: Mine 5-star and 1-star reviews for exact customer phrases
Pull support ticket and chat transcripts for named objections
Run or commission 12 to 15 buyer interviews before a new product's copy
Mine site search and on-site search terms for buying language
Distill founder or brand video content into a compile document with an LLM
Log consent before contacting checkout abandoners for research
Read every research pass for surprises, not to confirm the team's own belief
Build one feature-and-benefit table per product line
Hunt the keystone fact and untold process facts behind a product
inputs: brand brain: reviews and support tickets
founder_sees: A short digest of what customers actually say, with quotes and where each one came from.

name: Build and refresh buyer personas
what: Builds and updates data-grounded buyer personas from customer language rather than demographic labels, and opens a new persona once the main one plateaus.
encompasses: Draft personas by hand from the research packet's own language
Run one AI expansion round, validated against real quotes
Retire a persona once its ads stop converting
Open a new persona or use-case facet once the current one plateaus
Tag each persona with its own vocabulary and objections
outputs: persona records (belief, vocabulary, objections, plateau status)
founder_sees: A short list of who is being sold to right now, and why the next persona is being opened.

name: Define ad angles, appeals and positioning
what: Turns the research packet and product facts into a small set of testable angles, each one sentence for one persona, holding one dominant appeal, one buying question and one true point of difference.
encompasses: Write the one-sentence angle for one persona and one problem
Write the buying question: the belief the reader holds now and the belief they need
Pick the one dominant appeal the product can credibly satisfy
Default to cure-and-reward framing over prevention
Name the real rival as a habit or an old way, never a competitor brand
Check that no rival could honestly claim the same unique mechanism
Set story depth and appeal strength by awareness stage
Keep one idea per SKU or collection, never one idea for the whole store
Slow the agitation and widen self-identification for luxury or high-ticket goods
inputs: brand brain: products and claims tiers
outputs: angle brief (persona, problem, appeal, buying question, mechanism)
founder_sees: The one-sentence angle plan behind a coming batch of ads, in plain words.

name: Build and grade hook banks
what: Writes and grades opening hooks for cold video, VSL and static ads, and multiplies a working hook into layered variants across audio, on-screen copy and visual.
encompasses: Write hooks that name the persona's problem before the product
Grade each hook for clarity, relevance, novelty, specificity and credibility
Vary hooks across angle, offer, persona and format
Keep the product name, image and offer out of a cold hook
Check a curiosity hook against a real payoff before use
Multiply one working hook into audio, copy and visual variants
Clear rights before using a famous face or trending audio in a hook
Open a hook with the problem, adding a persona label only if it widens relevance
outputs: hook bank grouped by angle and format
founder_sees: The hooks going into next week's tests, and why each one was written that way.

name: Generate and test headline and primary-text sets
what: Writes headline and primary-text variant sets for statics, search and marketplace placements, each with a true specific and checked against length and image fit.
encompasses: Write a bank of 10 or more headline candidates before choosing 3
Put a true number, time, count or price in the headline
Keep headlines to 12 words or fewer, prefer the shorter option
Run the what-is-sold test on the headline alone
Test the headline against the real image before shipping
Generate headline variants from a bank of proven opener words
Keep product-shot headlines to 5 or 6 words that beat the current alternative
outputs: headline and primary-text variant set, by placement
founder_sees: The exact headline options for a coming ad, each with why it should work.

name: Write standardized concept and creative briefs
what: Writes the one-page creative brief, persona, angle, offer, destination, awareness stage, before any design tool or shoot is booked, using the same fixed fields every time.
encompasses: Fill the fixed brief fields: persona, problem, angle, offer, destination, format, stage
Confirm the click destination matches the offer before sign-off
Write a reusable copy skeleton for a catalogue brand's product line
Write the 3-part reader, belief, line brief before drafting any ad
Write a one-paragraph messaging strategy before a new product's copy
Keep hook, image, copy and destination at the same awareness stage
founder_sees: The one-page brief that will drive the next batch of ads.

name: Write static ad production briefs and generate variants
what: Writes the design brief for a static ad, eye path, image-headline pairing, primary-text weight, and produces image concepts and variants through the creative studio from a reference image, a winning ad or the real product photo.
encompasses: Give every static three jobs: stop the scroll, say the message, drive the click
Pick clarity or curiosity for a static, never the middle
Design the eye path so the highest-awareness message lands first
Give primary text and headline equal weight to the image
Avoid a plain white-background product shot for cold traffic
Scale a proven static by swapping one element, not the whole format
Drop the corner logo unless it is a deliberate native reveal
Generate variants from a pasted reference image or a competitor layout, layout and mood only
Keep the real product photo in any AI-touched image where accuracy matters
founder_sees: The static ad concept and a first-pass image to react to.

name: Write video ad scripts and storyboards
what: Scripts cold video, VSL and testimonial-style ads in the proven order, hook, bridge, mechanism, product, proof, objection, CTA, and storyboards the shot list, sized to how much education the product actually needs.
encompasses: Build a VSL only when the product needs real education to convert
Script the VSL in 7 parts from hook to CTA
Start length short and cut down further, not the reverse
Keep a clear CTA on the first VSL rather than testing no CTA
Bridge to education before naming the product
Reveal the product only as slowly as the awareness stage allows
Stack proof after the product and match it to the viewer
Close with a reason to buy, a risk reversal and one CTA with no open loop
Fix the opening of an underperforming video before the back half
Edit pace to match the format's polish level
Use a numbered-reasons body for routine, consumable products
founder_sees: The full script for a new video ad, with the reason for each section.

name: Write founder-led and authority-driven ad scripts
what: Scripts founder and creator-authority ads as an argument for the viewer's problem, never a biography, using only real, permissioned stories and reviews, and diversifies scenes so one founder does not fatigue the whole account.
encompasses: Build the founder script as claim, proof, mechanism, proof, CTA
Keep the founder story to origin, mechanism and the adversarial angle only
Tell it through the viewer's problem, not the founder's biography
Verify the founder story and reviews are real and unaltered before use
Diversify founder ads by scene, format and involvement level
Borrow category authority when there is no famous face
Test swapping the face before scaling a founder ad on cold traffic
Test removing the founder to open a new audience
Use matching customer proof instead of founder self-vouching
Put a real, named person behind founder-led copy, never an invented authority
founder_sees: The founder script, with which facts in it are real and sourced.

name: Build UGC and creator sourcing briefs
what: Writes the creator brief, never UGC without a concept, sets the vetting bar from past creator work, and tracks usage rights so a whitelisted post or licensed clip does not run past its window.
encompasses: Give every UGC ask a concept, not just an instruction to make content
Brief creators in detail, allow up to 2 takes
Vet a new creator by the brief behind their best past post
Choose a wide brief for discovery or a specific one for replication
Run partnership or whitelisted ads only through a page that already posts well
Log usage rights, scope and expiry per creator asset
Build and maintain a standing creator roster
founder_sees: The brief a creator would receive, and which rights are about to lapse.

name: Select and craft native platform formats
what: Picks a native TikTok- or Reels-style format from the product's actual trait, not a trend, and writes it so it does not read as an ad, matching the platform's own editorial style.
encompasses: Pick a native format by product trait: demo, transformation or POV
Write paid content in the platform's native editorial style
Judge a native video by purchases per view, not by views
founder_sees: Which native format was picked for a video ad, and why.

name: Direct product photography and image accuracy
what: Sets direction for product photography and any AI-touched image so the product shown matches what arrives at home, and points a photographed person's gaze toward the CTA.
encompasses: Require the real product photo in any AI-assisted image where accuracy matters
Check proof imagery is recognizable and true to the shipped product
Direct eye-line and gaze toward the CTA in a shot with a person
founder_sees: A short note on what the product shot must show accurately.

name: Build the offer as a creative and copy lever
what: Writes the offer itself, bundle, guarantee, urgency, value stack, trial, tiered ladder, as a lever the creative and copy can use, always checked against what operations can actually honor.
encompasses: Treat the offer as a concept lever, not just a discount
Word a bundle or kit as inclusion, real saving, and why-together in one line
Write the strongest guarantee operations can honor, placed at the decision point
Use a deadline only when it is real, stated in digits
Build a real, computed value stack so believed value beats price
Limit a special offer to a group the buyer plausibly belongs to
Offer a free trial on request over a part-price sample
Build a three-tier offer ladder from entry product to premium tier
Gate a discount behind email capture at exit intent
Bundle a low-ticket item when unit price cannot cover ad cost
outputs: offer construction note for the idea record
founder_sees: The exact offer wording and the operational limit it must not cross.

name: Run claim, policy and compliance checks
what: Checks every claim, testimonial, guarantee line and comparison in a creative or copy set against the brand record's claim tiers and current platform policy before it ships, and flags anything that cannot be traced to evidence.
encompasses: Never invent a number, study, count or as-seen-in claim
Verify an impressive claim against a document or test on file
Check each claim type against current platform ad policy
Keep testimonials real, permitted in writing and unaltered in meaning
Match guarantee wording exactly to the brand record's eligibility limits
Disclose paid partnerships, never present a brand page as independent
Replace graphic before-after imagery with an illustrated version for sensitive claims
Run a policy check on any line implying a personal attribute
Run the reasonable-reader test on figurative headline language
Produce a full claim-audit table before a set ships
Clear rights before using a famous face or trending term
inputs: brand brain: claims tiers (approved, site-backed, forbidden)
founder_sees: The claim audit table, with anything unresolved called out before it ships.

name: Diagnose creative fatigue and plan revivals
what: Tells apart a genuinely worn-out ad from a small persona pool, then revives a fatigued winner with a new hook or format swap before commissioning a whole new concept.
encompasses: Diagnose fatigue as audience exhaustion versus a small persona pool
Revive with new-footage hooks on the same body first
Rotate format, not just hooks, when a winner fatigues
Keep a real swing in every iteration, plus some net-new concepts every batch
Split a fatigued testimonial into a new hook with the old customer body
Move a strong mid-ad line to the hook as a cheap retest
Keep a winner running until its own numbers decline, then swap execution, not the appeal
founder_sees: Which ads are fatiguing and the exact fix planned, not a request for a whole new concept.

name: Break down and analyze own ad winners and losers
what: Breaks every winner and loser into its parts, hook, structure, proof, offer, CTA, with a written hypothesis for why it worked or did not, using the account's own numbers, not last-click ROAS alone.
encompasses: Read the full chain: attention, click, post-click, incremental result
Check CTR against link CTR before trusting a high click rate
Rank ads by spend first, then require the result to hold
Judge winners on incremental or 7-day-click results at ad-set level
Judge total portfolio profit, not the single best ROAS
Assign each surviving ad a funnel role from its real metrics
Run a frame-by-frame teardown on a live video before fixing it
Grade a draft against a rubric built from the account's own winners
Reskin a winning structure with new facts, never clone it
Check a winning format fits the new topic before reusing it
Find the natural break point between a winners pile and a losers pile
When an ad fails, change the headline first, then price, then offer
founder_sees: Why each strong or weak ad performed the way it did, in plain words with the numbers.

name: Design and structure creative and copy tests
what: Sets up every creative or copy test with a written hypothesis, a clean ad-set structure, a pre-set winner definition and a minimum read window, and sizes the test from the account's own traffic.
encompasses: Give every test a written hypothesis before it launches
Keep one persona-and-angle pair per ad set for a clean read
Size a pack to 4 to 8 ads, plan 10 or more per concept, with a short guaranteed-delivery window
Wait at least 7 days before judging a new pack, and record a low-delivery batch as inconclusive, not failed
Exclude existing customers from cold tests
Change one variable per test, sized big enough to measure, judged by cost per purchase
Cap per-ad delivery so one ad does not starve the rest
Treat a 1-element ad, headline-only, image-only, as a test, not a default
Check LTV or category-education cost before funding a test at scale
Run a small representative test before scaling any new offer or claim
Embed a hidden verification phrase to measure real read-through
Compare total sales, not just share shift, when testing a promotion
outputs: test brief (hypothesis, structure, size, read point, winner rule)
founder_sees: The test plan, and exactly how a winner will be called before it launches.

name: Plan and monitor the creative production pipeline and portfolio
what: Runs creative as a monthly pipeline, research, concept, build, variations, feedback, launch, sizes volume and budget from the account's own hit rate, and watches portfolio breadth and stage weight so no single ad or stage dominates.
encompasses: Run the pipeline in the fixed order every cycle
Size monthly volume from the account's own historical hit rate
Set a production budget tier, then replace it with real per-ad profit
Split effort mostly toward iteration, with some net-new always in the mix
Weight new creative at least 70% toward less-aware stages
Run several distinct formats at once, not one
Keep the portfolio diverse enough that the platform serves different shoppers
Track live coverage against the account's own tier defaults
Pace how hard a winner is pushed by inventory and cash, not ROAS alone
Tag the live library and find segment-by-format gaps
Weight the appeal mix by proven pull, keeping any appeal paying at least half the best
Start with organic content before scaling paid for a brand-new store
founder_sees: How much creative to make this month, and where the current library has gaps.

name: Select ad format and compare format economics
what: Chooses the ad format after the concept is set, using the product's education and demo needs, and compares formats by expected profit per ad rather than ROAS alone.
encompasses: Pick the format only after the concept, using the education and demo test
Test new angles and offers as statics before building video
Compare formats by expected gross profit per ad, not ROAS alone
Stop putting cold budget behind product-aware creative formats
Decide the click destination before the format for marketplace-heavy sellers
Note where a short campaign-budget push fits versus the default ad-set budget
founder_sees: Which format was picked for a concept, and the profit reasoning behind it.

name: Maintain naming, tagging and platform-spec standards
what: Keeps a fixed naming and tagging taxonomy for every asset, concept, persona, angle, offer, format, stage, source, and a live sheet of each ad platform's current character limits and truncation points.
encompasses: Tag every asset by concept, persona, angle, offer, format, stage and source
Tag creative by awareness stage at the moment it is built
Fetch and store current platform character limits before writing to them
Keep a stable creative ID that survives across platforms and file versions
Use controlled vocabulary and a fixed field order for campaign, ad set and ad names
founder_sees: Nothing directly. This keeps every other output consistent and searchable.

name: Govern AI use in the creative and copy pipeline
what: Sets where AI is allowed in the pipeline, drafting and grunt work, never final ideation or unsupervised authorship, grounds every AI draft in the brand's own facts and winners, and screens AI output for tells before it ships.
encompasses: Use AI in the middle of the pipeline, keep ideation and final judgment human
Load the brand's own facts and past winners into any AI tool before generating
Write the hook first, let AI draft the rest, hand-edit before a human editor cuts video
Ground AI-generated hooks in the brand's own winning ads
Screen AI-drafted scripts and lines for AI tells before finalizing
Let AI draft and improve lines, never let it author copy or supply proof unsupervised
Use founder or in-house content as the human counter to an AI-heavy creative mix
outputs: AI-tell screening pass on a draft
founder_sees: Nothing directly. This is a QA rule the agent applies to its own drafts.

name: Localise creative and copy for market and device
what: Specs creative and copy for a mobile-first, non-US market, vertical-only formats, dual-language hooks where needed, and local payment and delivery trust facts drawn from the brand record.
encompasses: Spec vertical-only, dual-language hooks for mobile-first markets
State local payment and delivery trust facts (COD, EMI, local carriers) from the brand record
Check that any translated or localised line still passes the claim and reading-level rules
inputs: brand brain: payment and delivery policies
outputs: localisation spec for a creative brief
founder_sees: The local facts and format choices built into a brief for this market.

name: Flag catalogue and dynamic product ad (DPA) creative risks
what: Checks the product feed and catalogue template before a DPA or catalog-retargeting layer goes live, and flags dirty data, missing overlays or a template that will misfire on accuracy.
encompasses: Flag catalog and DPA creative risks: feed quality, overlay template, SKU threshold, before handoff
Recommend a catalog retargeting layer run under handcrafted bottom-funnel objection ads, not alone
Check that custom overlays and lifestyle imagery are in place rather than a bare default catalog pull
inputs: brand brain: product catalogue and feed
founder_sees: Whether the product catalogue is ready for dynamic ads, and what would break first.

name: Build objection-handling and retargeting continuity copy
what: Writes one bottom-funnel ad or line per real objection pulled from customer data, prefaces the most common one early rather than saving it all for an FAQ, and keeps the same argument alive across every follow-up and retargeting touch.
encompasses: Build one bottom-of-funnel ad per objection, not a benefit list
Add fit, sizing and returns risk to the apparel objection list
Preface a real objection early, keep the full FAQ at the bottom
Address the three blockers for a warm list: risk, price, effectiveness
Pre-empt a rival's pitch with true facts (inoculation), using a weak attack only
Reposition against a self-image or identity objection
Continue the same specific argument through every follow-up or retargeting message
Personalize a lead follow-up to exactly what they asked about, with local proof
founder_sees: The objection each bottom-funnel ad answers, sourced from real customer words.

name: Design channel and destination routing for ad traffic
what: Decides where a given ad should send traffic, site, off-platform marketplace search, or a single shared front-end offer, so acquisition channels are not competing for different destinations.
encompasses: Route a no-CTA, top-of-funnel VSL's viewers to marketplace search rather than a purchase page
Point several acquisition channels at one shared front-end offer instead of fragmenting the pitch
Confirm the chosen destination is reachable and matches the ad's promise before sign-off
founder_sees: Which destination a given ad or channel should point to, and why.

name: Apply core direct-response copywriting rules across formats
what: Applies the account's fixed copywriting rules, reading level, sentence and paragraph pacing, single-idea discipline, proof ranking, framing defaults, to any ad, page or email line, regardless of surface.
encompasses: Run the salesman test on every line before it ships
Open every sentence with the reader, never I, we, our or the brand name
Hit a 7th-grade reading score for a thumb scrolling a phone
Cut cleverness, jokes and boasting from sales copy by default
Keep one idea per sentence and one idea per asset
Structure the body as attention, interest, desire, proof, then action
Ladder every feature to a benefit in the product's own spec units
Swap vague quality words for a concrete, checkable detail
Rank proof by strength: demonstration, third-party evidence, cost narration, analogy
Default to positive framing, use negative only when the product fully resolves it
Reserve ALL CAPS for print packaging and inserts, avoid it in digital ads
outputs: copy set (headline, body, CTA) in the brand's plain-language style
founder_sees: The finished copy, already checked against the house style rules.

name: Write landing and product page copy blocks (message match)
what: Writes the page-level copy blocks, hero, benefit blocks, spec block, FAQ, in a fixed order so the ad's promise, the headline and the page all say the same thing, and checks the page for real friction before it ships.
encompasses: Reuse one headline promise across the ad, the PDP first line and the collection hero
Assemble the hero as eyebrow, headline, deck, one CTA
Build the page in a fixed order, with a CTA every 2 to 3 sections and FAQ last
Write a product page in three blocks: title, benefit bullets, spec block
Cut a spec bullet that answers no real shopper filter or search
Check ad-to-page congruency against the ad's exact promise
Run a heatmap or attention tool on a new page before launch
Build a timely page around a real, relevant news story, only when genuinely relevant
Make sure a quiz or interactive step delivers a real personalized result
founder_sees: The page copy next to the ad it must match, with any mismatch flagged.

name: Write marketplace listing copy
what: Front-loads a marketplace listing title with the product, key spec and use case, in that marketplace's own conventions, using the same claim tiers as ads.
encompasses: Order the title as product, key spec, use case
Write bullet points in the marketplace's accepted format
Align listing claims with the same brand claim tiers used in ads
founder_sees: The listing title and bullets, ready to hand to the team that publishes to the marketplace.

name: Write SMS ad and marketing copy
what: Writes SMS lines as one short message: the offer or update, one clear action, and the opt-out, within carrier and platform rules.
encompasses: Write the offer or update line at SMS length
Write one clear call to action
Include the required opt-out line
Check against current SMS marketing compliance rules
founder_sees: The SMS text exactly as it would send.

name: Write lifecycle email and retention copy blocks
what: Writes the copy blocks for lifecycle email and retention sends, subject and preview, structure choice, segmentation, cadence rules, so the Lifecycle specialist can build and schedule the actual flow.
encompasses: Pick the structure (PPAS, CJN, HSO or an outline block) before writing
Segment welcome emails by how the subscriber joined the list
Design a three-part system: welcome, sell, revive
Write a re-engagement line for subscribers inactive 30 to 60 days
Branch copy tone by engagement level (openers get sold faster)
Keep about 80% of sends plain-benefit, the rest for gimmick or urgency
Write a value email before the next promo, not promo after promo
Write a soft-sell P.S. line for value-only sends
Write a one-word reply CTA to gauge warm interest
Repeat the same CTA a second time in deadline emails
Write three closing-day emails at different times on the final sale day
Write a resend with a new subject after a launch email goes unopened
outputs: email and SMS copy blocks by lifecycle stage
founder_sees: The email copy for a flow, handed to Lifecycle to build and schedule.

name: Frame price and value in copy
what: Chooses how a price is framed in copy: charm versus round-number endings, cost-per-day reframes, and an honest reason stated whenever a price looks unusually low.
encompasses: Match price-ending style to positioning: charm pricing or round numbers
Reframe price as a small recurring cost per day or per use
State the honest reason when a price is unusually low
Use an apples-to-oranges comparison instead of an itemized value breakdown, when it is the fairer read
founder_sees: How a price is worded in copy, and why that framing was chosen.

name: Name products, brands and proprietary systems
what: Names a new product, method or proprietary system so the name itself carries the benefit or story, and attaches a real named person to an otherwise generic product.
encompasses: Draft name candidates that tell the benefit or story
Name a proprietary system so buyers compare methods, not commodities
Attach a real, named person to a generic product name
Test candidate names with small paid spend before committing
founder_sees: The name shortlist and the reasoning behind each one.

name: Research competitor creative and messaging, signal only
what: Studies competitor ads and messaging from public ad libraries for structure, cadence and gaps only, filters out likely paid or fake-organic content, and never copies text, logos, products or faces into the brand's own work.
encompasses: Audit competitor messaging for baseline and white noise
Check a competitor's ad library on a fixed weekly or twice-monthly cadence
Study competitors one or two revenue tiers above, one at a time
Study the brand's own winners first, then competitors, one at a time
Mine competitor video transcripts for angles, never wording
Filter out likely paid content before treating an organic post as a signal
Build a swipe file from niche brands' email and post-purchase flows
outputs: competitor signal report (structure and gaps, never claims)
founder_sees: What competitors are doing structurally, marked clearly as a signal, not a proven winner.

name: Edit and QA copy before handoff to the QA Gate
what: Runs the line-level and page-level edit pass on every draft, cutting, tightening and testing readability in code, before the set goes to the shared QA Gate.
encompasses: Rest the draft, then read it aloud until it stops stumbling
Cut every non-working word with a modifier sweep
Cut the lead, move the best line to the top
Run the tossed-salad audit, cutting any claim off the one idea
Score readability in code and shorten until it passes
Hold a 9-of-10 ship bar, get outside feedback first
Run the skim test: scroll without reading, check the offer still lands
Check voice consistency across a run of SKU or collection pages, 3 at a time
Preview a static in-context against real feed clutter before sign-off
Show reviewers 3 or more line versions, not just 1
Never leave a blank placeholder in client-facing copy
founder_sees: Nothing directly. This is the polish pass before the QA Gate and the founder ever see a set.
